data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Adonis was a handsome god and a favorite of Aphrodite. The name is derived from the Greek word adon, meaning 'lord' or 'master'. Adonis was a mortal man who was beloved by Aphrodite and was granted the gift of eternal resurrection after his death. The name Adonis carries the meaning “God, Lord” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Adonis usually hope their child will grow to embody god, lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adonis total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
data.cultural_impact: The name Adonis has been used by various Christian communities throughout history, particularly in the Eastern Orthodox Church. It is considered a unisex name in the Middle East and in some Christian traditions, although it is most commonly used for men. The name holds cultural significance in these traditions as a reminder of the physical beauty of Jesus Christ, with Adonis symbolizing the ideal male figure.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, Adonis represents the divine masculine and the power of resurrection. The name carries connotations of beauty, strength, and divine love. For Christians, Adonis can serve as a reminder of the sacrifice and resurrection of Jesus Christ, who is himself referred to as the "Lord" or "Master" in the Bible. Additionally, some Christians believe that the name Adonis can be a source of protection and strength, particularly in times of spiritual or emotional turmoil. Ultimately, the name Adonis reflects the power and beauty of the divine, inviting us to connect with the deeper spiritual truths of our faith.
